name: Alexandra Trusova
nicknameReason: Earned for her explosive skating speed, high-flying jump power, and pioneering quadruple jump layouts in women's singles.
bio: Single skater who introduced multiple quadruple jump types into international women's competition, becoming the first woman to land the quad Lutz, quad Flip, and quad Toe Loop in ISU events. At the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics, she executed five quadruple jumps in her free skate to win the silver medal.
achievements: 2022 Olympic Winter Games (Beijing) — Silver Medalist, Women's Singles
2021 ISU World Championships (Stockholm) — Bronze Medalist
2022 ISU European Championships — Silver Medalist (2020 Bronze)
2018 & 2019 ISU World Junior Championships — Two-time Gold Medalist
First woman to land five quadruple jumps in an Olympic free skate (2022)

name: Alysa Liu
bio: American single skater who became the youngest U.S. women's national champion at age 13 in 2019 and the first U.S. woman to land a quadruple jump in international competition. After returning from a brief retirement in 2024, she won the 2025 World Championship and 2026 Olympic women's singles title.
achievements: 2026 Olympic Winter Games (Milano Cortina) — Gold Medalist, Women's Singles & Team Event
2025 ISU World Championships (Boston) — Gold Medalist (2022 Bronze)
2025–26 ISU Grand Prix Final — Gold Medalist
2019 & 2020 U.S. National Championships — Two-time Gold Medalist

name: Ilia Malinin
nicknameReason: Adopted as his signature moniker after becoming the first skater to land a ratified quadruple Axel in competition and executing seven-quad programs.
bio: American men's single skater who made figure skating history in September 2022 by landing the first ratified quadruple Axel in international competition. He has won three consecutive ISU World Championships (2024–2026) and multiple Grand Prix Final titles.
achievements: 2026 Olympic Winter Games (Milano Cortina) — Gold Medalist, Team Event
2024, 2025 & 2026 ISU World Championships — Three-time Gold Medalist
2023, 2024 & 2025 ISU Grand Prix Final — Three-time Gold Medalist
2023–2026 U.S. National Championships — Four-time Gold Medalist
First skater to land a ratified Quadruple Axel (4A) in ISU competition (2022)

name: Kaori Sakamoto
nicknameReason: Given by skating media early in her senior career for her explosive speed and high-trajectory jumps.
bio: Japanese single skater noted for high ice coverage, deep running edges, and sustained competitive consistency across three Olympic cycles. She became the first woman since Peggy Fleming to win three consecutive ISU World titles (2022–2024) and added a fourth World title in 2026.
achievements: 2026 Olympic Winter Games (Milano Cortina) — Silver Medalist, Women's Singles & Team Event
2022 Olympic Winter Games (Beijing) — Bronze Medalist (Singles) & Silver Medalist (Team)
2022, 2023, 2024 & 2026 ISU World Championships — Four-time Gold Medalist (2025 Silver)
2023–24 ISU Grand Prix Final — Gold Medalist
2018 ISU Four Continents Championships — Gold Medalist

name: Yuzuru Hanyu
nicknameReason: Frequently used by media and commentators in reference to his classical posture, musicality, and presentation on the ice.
bio: Japanese men's single skater who won back-to-back Olympic gold medals in 2014 and 2018, becoming the first man in 66 years to defend an Olympic figure skating title. In 2020, he became the first male single skater to complete the career Super Slam across all major ISU junior and senior championships.
achievements: 2014 Sochi & 2018 PyeongChang Olympic Winter Games — Two-time Gold Medalist
2014 & 2017 ISU World Championships — Two-time Gold Medalist (7 total World medals)
2013–2016 ISU Grand Prix Final — Four-time consecutive Gold Medalist
2020 ISU Four Continents Championships — Gold Medalist (Career Super Slam)
First skater to land a quadruple Loop (4Lo) in international competition (2016)

name: Shoma Uno
bio: Japanese men's single skater who became the first athlete to land a quadruple Flip in international competition in 2016. A three-time Olympic medalist and six-time Japanese national champion, he also became the first Japanese man to win consecutive ISU World titles in 2022 and 2023.

2019 ISU Four Continents Championships — Gold Medalist

name: Yuma Kagiyama
bio: Japanese men's single skater recognized for fluid edge quality, speed across the ice, and consistent podium finishes at major championships. He earned individual and team silver medals at both the 2022 Beijing and 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympics.

name: Amber Glenn
bio: American single skater known for landing the triple Axel in international competition and winning three consecutive U.S. national titles from 2024 to 2026. She captured the 2024–25 ISU Grand Prix Final title and earned an Olympic team gold medal at Milano Cortina 2026.

name: Junhwan Cha
nicknameReason: Used by South Korean media for his graceful skating style and background as a former child actor before focusing on figure skating.
bio: South Korean men's single skater who became the first male skater from South Korea to win an ISU Championship title at the 2022 Four Continents and a World Championship medal in 2023. Across three Winter Olympic appearances, he placed 15th in 2018, 5th in 2022, and 4th in 2026.

name: Evgeni Plushenko
nicknameReason: Called The Snow King for his dominant championship reign and regal programs, while Plushy is an affectionate shortening of his surname.
bio: Russian men's single skater who competed across four Winter Olympic Games from 2002 to 2014, winning four Olympic medals to tie Gillis Grafström's all-time figure skating record. He also captured three ISU World Championship titles, seven European titles, and four Grand Prix Finals.

bio: Russian men's single skater who won the 2002 Salt Lake City Olympic gold medal with his iconic free skate to The Man in the Iron Mask. During the 2001–02 season, he became the first skater to sweep the Grand Prix Final, European Championships, World Championships, and Olympic Games in a single season.

nicknameReason: Earned the moniker for his consistency and mastery of quadruple jumps, becoming the first skater to land five quads in one program and six across an Olympic free skate.
bio: American men's single skater who won the 2022 Beijing Olympic gold medal and three consecutive ISU World Championships from 2018 to 2021. He also won six straight U.S. national titles (2017–2022) and three consecutive Grand Prix Final crowns.

nicknameReason: Popularized by her 2017–18 Olympic gold medal free skate to Don Quixote, which she performed in a signature red ballet tutu.
bio: Russian single skater who won women's singles gold at the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics and completed the career Super Slam with her 2019 World Championship victory. Her back-loaded 2018 Olympic jump layout prompted the ISU to revise its second-half bonus rules.

name: Kamila Valieva
nicknameReason: Used by commentators and fans for her posture, flexibility, and technical precision during her junior and early 2021 senior seasons.
bio: Russian single skater who won the 2020 World Junior Championship and 2021 Grand Prix titles at Skate Canada and Rostelecom Cup, becoming the first woman to surpass 90 points in a short program. In 2024, CAS issued a four-year ban retroactive to December 25, 2021, disqualifying her subsequent 2022 European and Beijing Olympic results.
